results.text: Comparative note.WikiSQL tests large-scale, single-table translation with limited SQL syntax, whereas Spider and BIRD evaluate full SQL expressivity and cross-schema generalization, together covering the breadth of Text-to-SQL challenges. 3.3 Conversational and Context-Dependent Benchmarks To address real-world dialogue scenarios, two conversational benchmarks extend Spider with multi-turn interactions: • SParC[ 91]: 4,298 coherent question sequences comprising more than 12K questions over Spider schemas, testing context retention, coreference resolution, and incremental query composition. • CoSQL[ 90]: a large-scale, cross-domain conversational Text-to-SQL benchmark comprising over 3,000 user–system dialogues (30,000+ turns) and 10,000+ annotated SQL queries across 200 complex databases spanning 138 domains.

• Spider-DK[ 21] andSpider-Syn[ 23]: Spider extensions that introduce domain-knowledge requirements and synonym substitutions, respectively, to further challenge generalization. • WikiTableQuestions[ 58]: a semi-structured table QA benchmark with 22,033 hand-crafted question–answer pairs over Wikipedia tables (each with at least 8 rows and 5 columns). Unlike templated datasets, it exhibits high linguistic variability across nearly 4,000 unique column headers and many domains. Tasks include table lookup, aggregation, superlatives (argmax/argmin), arithmetic, and set operations, making it a useful testbed for Text-to-SQL systems on semi-structured data. • LiveSQLBench[ 4] andBIRD-Interact[ 36]: LiveSQLBench is a contamination-free, continuously updated benchmark from the BIRD team that supports the full spectrum of SQL operations (including DML and DDL) and organizes external knowledge as a hierarchical knowledge base whose entries depend on one another.

• BIRD[ 47] (BIg Bench for laRge-scale Database-grounded Text-to-SQL evaluation): a crossdomain benchmark designed to stress-test models on large, heterogeneous schemas and substantial data volumes. Here,cross-domainrefers to coverage of a wide variety of professional fields and database schemas, ranging from sports and finance to healthcare, blockchain, and education, so that evaluation is not biased toward any single domain. BIRD comprises 12,751 unique question–SQL pairs over 95 real-world databases totaling 33.4 GB of relational data, spanning 37 professional domains, and evaluates parser robustness against schema complexity, data scale, and domain variability. • UNITE[ 44] (A Unified Benchmark for Text-to-SQL Evaluation): UNITE assembles and normalizes eighteen public Text-to-SQL datasets into a single unified format to evaluate generalization across diverse schemas, SQL patterns, and domains.

This metric is easy to compute and interpret but is rigid: semantically equivalent queries (e.g., queries that differ only in predicate order) receive a score of 0 even though they return the same result. For example, the following two queries are semantically equivalent but fail exact match: 9

The reward is deliberately simple: 1 if the query’s execution result matches the gold result, 0.1 if the query is syntactically valid and executes but returns a different result, and 0 otherwise. Combined with carefully filtered training data, strong supervised initialization (from OmniSQL checkpoints), and online training, this simple reward lets the model handle SQL aliasing and semantically equivalent variants naturally, and even the 7B variant matches earlier 70B-class systems. Databricks RLVR-32B: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards.Databricks Mosaic Research advanced Text-to-SQL reasoning through reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) [1, 16]. Unlike approaches that depend on proxy or learned reward models, RLVR exploits rewards derived directly from the correctness of SQL execution, simplifying the training pipeline and grounding supervision in the task itself.

Additional structure-oriented metrics used in practice include: • Component Matching (CM).Used in the Spider benchmark, CM breaks each SQL query into its main components, including SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY , ORDER BY , and keywords. For each component, it computes an F1 score between the predicted and ground-truth sets of sub-components while ignoring order. This enables fine-grained analysis of which parts of a query are generated correctly. • Exact Set Match (EM without values).Also used in Spider, this metric evaluates structural equivalence by treating the tables, columns, and operators within each clause as unordered sets and ignoring constant values. By focusing on structure rather than surface form, it credits semantically equivalent rewrites even when literal values differ. 13

results.text: Methodology.SQL2NL (i) ingests a gold SQL query and its schema description; (ii) prompts a generation model with constraints that encourage lexical and syntactic diversity while forbidding schemaidentifier leakage; (iii) validates paraphrase fidelity through automatic embedding-based checks and targeted human review of a sample; and (iv) evaluates NL-to-SQL systems by comparing execution accuracy on the original questions with that on the SQL2NL paraphrases. The framework supports weighted (human-adjusted) scoring so that low-quality paraphrases do not unduly penalize systems. SQL2NL can also produce augmented training data for robustness-oriented fine-tuning. Evaluation protocol and datasets.The authors apply SQL2NL to Spider and BIRD and stratify their analyses by query complexity (number of joins, nested clauses, and aggregates). The primary metrics are execution accuracyand therobustness gap, defined as the drop in execution accuracy from the original to the paraphrased questions.

results.text: 4.3 Evaluating Robustness via SQL2NL: Schema-Aligned Paraphrasing The SQL2NL framework [69] proposes a schema-aware approach to measure and improve therobustness of NL-to-SQL systems under lexical and syntactic variation. Rather than paraphrasing natural language questions naïvely (which can inadvertently change schema links), SQL2NL generates paraphrases conditioned on thegold SQLand the target database schema, producing diverse utterances that preserve the original intent while keeping schema alignment intact. This makes it possible to measure how sensitive a model is to wording, independently of schema-linking errors.

results.text: (TSED). These metrics quantify both clause-level accuracy and the structural fidelity of predicted queries with respect to reference queries. SQL Query Analysis Metric (SQAM).SQAM decomposes each SQL query into its principal clauses: SELECT, FROM, WHERE, GROUP BY , HAVING, and ORDER BY . For every clause, the overlap between the predicted and reference sub-clauses is measured with precision, recall, and a weighted F1 score; semantically important clauses such as SELECT and WHERE receive higher weight in the final aggregation. In contrast to string-based metrics such as BLEU, SQAM penalizes omitted predicates, incorrect join conditions, and inappropriate aggregation choices, and therefore provides a more informative signal of partial correctness. Tree Similarity of Editing Distance (TSED).TSED compares the abstract syntax trees (ASTs) of the generated and reference queries.

Both queries are parsed into trees, and an edit distance is computed over node insertions, deletions, and substitutions; this distance is normalized by the size of the larger tree and converted into a similarity score in [0,1] (e.g., 1−normalized distance ). Because it operates on the AST, TSED captures hierarchical and structural similarity and rewards outputs that are structurally correct even when superficial token ordering or aliasing differs. Empirically, TSED correlates strongly with execution accuracy and is therefore a useful proxy when direct execution against the target database is not possible. Practical significance.SQAM and TSED form a complementary evaluation framework: SQAM focuses on clause-level and compositional correctness, whereas TSED captures global structural alignment. Used jointly, they provide a more robust assessment of model quality than either alone.

answer: Test-suite accuracy checks whether the predicted query matches the gold query’s result across every database in a curated suite designed to expose diverse logical edge cases.
